subject: Audit provenance & export options for admin activity logs (SOC 2 / SIG)
messages:
From: Claire Jennings <claire.j@acmebiotech.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@acmebiotech.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Audit evidence ask — admin activity provenance and export format

Hi Vanessa,

We're preparing for our upcoming SOC 2 audit and the SIG review. The auditor has asked for detailed provenance for admin activity logs (who did what, when, and how the exports were generated). Specifically they want:

- A description of exactly what events are recorded for admin actions (console, API, role changes, token creation/rotation, policy changes).
- The schema and sample export (fields + sample rows) and the export file's checksum.
- Retention policy: default retention and options for 1/2/3+ years, and how deletions are handled.
- Chain-of-custody for evidence handed to third-party auditors (signed manifest, hashing, timestamps).
- Whether we can stream logs to our S3 bucket in near real time (encrypted at rest in buyer's account).

I've attached the questionnaire (security_questionnaire_v3.pdf). Can you share a sample export and brief provenance write-up by EOD Tuesday? If you prefer, we'll set a 30-min call to walk through details.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Jennings
Senior Compliance Manager
Acme Biotech

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Claire Jennings <claire.j@acmebiotech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit evidence ask — admin activity provenance and export format

Claire —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary of what we can provide and next steps:

What we log (high level): console sign-ins (actor id, method, IP, geo), admin API calls (endpoint, params metadata, response code), role/permission changes (actor, target identity, before/after), key/KMS operations (create/rotate/delete), model-deploy actions, and export job operations (initiator, manifest, checksums).

Export formats and delivery:
- Ad-hoc exports: gzipped JSONL (row per event) or CSV (flattened) with export manifest (export_manifest_20260830.json) that includes SHA256 checksums for each file.
- Bulk snapshots (for longer retention snapshots): parquet or tar.gz bundles with per-file checksums and an overall signed manifest.
- Streaming: for Dedicated and Private deployments we support streaming to customer S3 (server-side encrypted). For Hosted customers we offer scheduled export jobs; near-real-time push can be enabled via a connector (requires onboarding).

Retention: default on Hosted is 365 days for admin activity by policy. Dedicated/Private can be configured at provisioning time for extended retention (2+ years) and we support customer-requested archived snapshots for compliance. Deletions are logical + physical purge after retention; purge operations are logged and included in export manifests.

Chain-of-custody: we produce an export manifest with file-level SHA256, export job timestamp, initiating actor id, and a Redwoodsigned statement of receipt. For Private, we can optionally sign manifests with customer-provided KMS keys.

I've attached a small sample export manifest and a 10-line sample extract for your review (export_manifest_20260830.json). I'll follow up with Marissa to include the chain-of-custody template and technical details on hashing + signature. If you want a call, propose available times and we'll lock one in.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Audit evidence ask — admin activity provenance and export format

Hi Claire — adding a few technical details from the evidence packaging side: 

- Hashing and integrity: exports include per-file SHA256 and a manifest hash. We also generate a signing blob that our platform signs with our evidence key (and, for Private customers, we can sign with your KMS key on request). That lets auditors verify the export hasn't been tampered with.

- Event ordering & monotonicity: event IDs include a server-generated monotonic sequence plus wall-clock timestamp; exports preserve sequence to allow re-play and tamper-detection.

- Identifiers & PII: actor identifiers in hosted exports are internal IDs; on request we can map to canonical user emails for audit packages, or pseudonymize.

- Chain-of-custody packet: PDF manifest (chain_of_custody_stub.pdf) + export bundle + checksums + signature. We include the export job record (who initiated, IP, job id) and the transport record (S3 PUT location, timestamp).

- Retention/restore: For Dedicated/Private customers we recommend a locked archive tier with snapshotting every 30 days; restores include an audit of snapshots and a signed restore manifest.

If you can confirm whether Acme prefers manifest signed by Redwood only vs. dual-signed (Redwood + Acme KMS), I can prepare the chain-of-custody packet and a sample proof package for your auditor.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal, Product Security
Redwood Inference
Attaching: chain_of_custody_stub.pdf (template for audit manifest)

3) We will need a DPA addendum (DocuSign) for any retention extension / streaming agreement. I've attached a draft (acme_dpa_addendum_draft.docx).

Claire

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Audit evidence ask — admin activity provenance and export format

Claire —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Short answers and next steps: 

- Retention: Hosted customers can request bespoke retention (2 years) via a compliance addendum; we'll run an export cadence (monthly snapshots) and keep a 2-year shard in cold storage. For predictable SLAs we recommend Dedicated or Private, which can be configured at provisioning with native long-term retention.

- Streaming/SSE-KMS: Near-real-time streaming with SSE-KMS to your S3 is currently available for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we can enable a managed connector that delivers on a "low-latency" schedule (near-real-time is treated as a special onboarding; estimated 2–4 weeks to validate and approve). For Acme, we can do a dual-signed manifest and configure SSE-KMS with your key during connector onboarding.

- DocuSign / DPA: happy to take the draft. I'll loop Legal/Finance to expedite the addendum review — please upload the Doc to the shared drive link (or I can pull it from the email).

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm whether you want dual-signing (Redwood + Acme KMS) for manifests.
2) If yes, we'll prepare chain-of-custody packet and a sample signed export within 48 hours.
3) If you want near-real-time streaming, we'll start the connector intake; schedule 30-min kickoff.

I'm available Wed 9/2 10:00 PT and have booked a tentative slot. If that works, we'll send an invite and include our Solutions engineer to cover the S3 connector details.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Security Operations
Redwood Inference
